name: Voltius
headline: An SSH client that has quietly grown into a local infrastructure cockpit.
standfirst: Voltius combines SSH, SFTP, serial, encrypted sync, containers, plugins and a local MCP server in a Rust/Tauri desktop app.
evidence: Repository, README and public project material. Toolglass has not installed or run Voltius.

body.heading: What is it?
paragraphs: Voltius starts as a modern SSH/SFTP client but extends into serial connections, persistent workspaces, encrypted device sync, container management, process monitoring, plugins and a local MCP server that can expose host and session operations to compatible AI tools.

body.heading: Why did Radar notice it?
paragraphs: The interesting part is not another pretty SSH tab. Voltius is trying to make remote-machine administration programmable without forcing credentials and host metadata into somebody else's cloud. Its Gist-based sync option encrypts locally, while the MCP integration is off by default and runs on the user's machine.
That combination makes it a useful example of where agent tooling may be heading: not agents replacing infrastructure software, but established tools growing carefully bounded machine interfaces.

body.heading: What's the catch?
paragraphs: The feature list is expanding quickly and the project still describes itself as early beta. macOS builds are not yet notarized and Windows builds are not yet code-signed, so first-run security warnings are expected. The MCP surface is powerful enough that its permission and audit behaviour deserves hands-on scrutiny before anyone lets an agent near production hosts.

body.heading: Who might want it?
paragraphs: Homelab users, developers and small infrastructure teams who want a Termius-style interface without making a hosted account the centre of gravity, especially if they are experimenting with agent-controlled operations.

verdict: An unusually ambitious open SSH client whose most interesting feature may be the boundary it is drawing between local credentials and agent-accessible infrastructure controls.
nextStep: Install it with a disposable VM, inspect the MCP permissions and audit trail, then test whether an agent can perform useful bounded tasks without gaining a dangerously broad shell shortcut.
